items.title: langchain-core==1.7.0
items.abstract_or_text: Changes since langchain-core==1.6.13 release(core): 1.7.0 (#41418) feat(core): emit `tool-call-delta` for streamed tool-call args (#41257) ## Notes - Tool-call args now stream as `tool-call-delta` slices instead of `block-delta` snapshots of the args so far. If you read raw stream events and their `block-delta` args mid-stream, read `tool-call-delta` instead. `.tool_calls.get()` and `.output` are unchanged. To keep snapshots, pin `langchain-core<1.7`. - Since 1.6.13, iterating `ChatModelStream.tool_calls` yields each call's new args slice, not a snapshot of the args so far.

items.abstract_or_text: llama-quant : fix 4D tensor quantization using ggml_nrows() and name-based expert detection (#30820) * llama-quant : fix quantizing 4D tensors nrows_total was ne[1]*ne[2], so for a 4D tensor only the first ne[2] slices were quantized and the rest of the rows were dropped. Use ggml_nrows(tensor) to count all rows, including ne[3]. Fixes #29916 * llama-quant : detect expert tensors by name and fix imatrix size for 4D tensors The MXFP4_MOE path used ne[2] > 1 to detect MoE expert tensors. This is wrong for non-expert tensors with 3 or more dims, e.g. MLA projections (BailingMoE3) and 4D conv kernels. Use the tensor name instead: all tensors used by GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID are named *_exps or *_chexps. This also removes the BailingMoE3 special case. The imatrix holds one vector of ne[0] values per 2D slice, so the expected size is ne[0]*ne[2]*ne[3], not ne[0]*ne[2]. This matches how the imatrix is indexed per row for 4D tensors in llama_tensor_quantize_impl. items.abstract_or_text: CUDA: fuse FFN gate/up matmuls and GLU in MMQ with interleaved gate/up rows (#29948) * cuda: fuse FFN gate/up and GLU in MMQ with interleaved gate/up rows For prompt processing, run the gate and up matmuls of a dense FFN as one mul_mat_q launch and apply the GLU in the write-back. - The loaders take the gate weights as a second pointer and fill the weight tile with up and gate rows interleaved in chunks of 8, so each thread holds an up value and the matching gate value (rows r and r + 8 of an MMA tile). - The MMA loop is unchanged: same tile, warp layout, vec_dot and one sum[] per thread. The fused write-back computes the GLU from registers and writes half the rows. - The fused path uses the regular tiling (no stream-k) with the column tiles innermost so that neighbouring blocks share weight tiles. - Enabled for Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0 and IQ4_XS on NVIDIA Turing and newer. * cuda: assert the fused MMQ gate argument and trim redundant comments * cuda: move the fused MMQ hint check to should_fuse and add TODOs * cuda: pass prec_src1 to the fused MMQ write-back * cuda: fuse only with efficient tiling and no fallback, merge the GLU write-back * cuda: require has_fusion explicitly, drop the fusion-only src1 precision check * cuda: launch the fused MMQ kernel through the stream-k kernel with one block per tile * cuda: inline the MMQ tiling-efficiency check * tests: one fused gate/up MMQ case per type and GLU op * cuda: always launch the fused MMQ kernel with one block per tile * tests: shorten the fused gate/up MMQ test comment * cuda: select the fused MMQ loader and write-back in ggml_cuda_mmq_get_util_funcs * cuda: run the fused MMQ kernel on the plain tiling path * cuda: put the column tiles innermost in the MMQ plain tiling path **Website:** - A request nested deep enough overflows the stack of the HTTP thread and llama-server dies (SIGBUS on macOS, SIGSEGV on Linux): for a tool schema from a few hundred levels on macOS and about 10000 on Linux. Check the depth first and answer 400 past 128 levels: the chat inputs in common_chat_templates_apply (tools, tool-call arguments, chat_template_kwargs, json_schema), the json_schema of /completion, and the whole /v1/systemone body. items.abstract_or_text: minimax-m3 : forward quant scales to the graph (fixes #31063) (#31097) The generic scale pass in llama-model.cpp loads the per-expert NVFP4 scale2 tensors (ffn_{up,gate,down}_exps_s) and the per-tensor MXFP8 scales for the dense FFN and the shared expert, but minimax-m3.cpp never forwarded any of them to the graph. build_moe_ffn() defaults these to nullptr, so build_lora_mm_id() skipped its w_s branch entirely and the routed-expert weights came out global_scale times too large, swamping the residual (reported G ~= 15123 for M3.1 Flash) and producing token soup. Forward all scale tensors at the three call sites, matching the pattern used by flint and the other NVFP4-capable MoE models. items.abstract_or_text: tests : add speculative rejection draft sampling test (#30213) * tests : add speculative rejection draft sampling test This commit adds a test for speculative rejection sampling test that excercises the speculative rejection sampling mechanism in common/speculative.cpp. The motivation for this is have a test that verifies that the speculative draft models emitts tokens that match the target models distribution. So when rejection sampling occurs it should still produce the same probability distribution as if we directly sampled from the target model. Running the test: ```console ctest --test-dir build -R "^test-speculative-rejection-sampling" \ --n_trials 5000 -V ``` This will generate two models, one target and one draft model. For subsequent runs use the "fixture exclude any" option to avoid recreating the models: ```console ctest --test-dir build-cpu-debug -R \ "^test-speculative-rejection-sampling" \ -FA "^speculative-models" --n_trails 5000 -V ``` * remove draft model **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: mtmd : lfm2 resize matches torchvision (#30943) * mtmd : lfm2 bilinear resize matches torchvision Lfm2VlImageProcessor and d1-omni vision.py resize uint8 images with torchvision (antialias=True). That is Pillow's algorithm, except that the weights are int16 with as many fractional bits as the largest weight allows, where Pillow uses 22 bits. The Pillow port was 1-2 levels off on about 1% of the values of the d1-omni and LFM2.5-VL crops. RESIZE_ALGO_BILINEAR_TORCH rounds the weights of the Pillow port to that precision and scales them back to 22 bits, which gives the output of torchvision with the same passes, and "bilinear" maps to it for LFM2 and d1-omni. Other models keep the Pillow algorithms. * mtmd : lfm2 bicubic resize matches torchvision Lfm2VlImageProcessor resizes with torchvision for the bicubic checkpoints too (d1-3B, LFM2-VL), so "bicubic" maps to RESIZE_ALGO_BICUBIC_TORCH for LFM2: the Pillow bicubic filter (a = -0.5, as torchvision with antialias) with the int16 weights of torchvision. The Pillow port was 1-2 levels off on about 0.25% of the values of the d1-3B crops. * use bitfield, add hparams setter --------- Co-authored-by: Xuan Son Nguyen **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** -
